response: Yes, receipt of hospice care in nursing homes can improve the management of pain at the end of life. According to the findings, nursing home residents enrolled in hospice care tend to have better analgesic management of daily pain compared to those not enrolled in hospice care. However, it's also noted that many dying nursing home residents in daily pain are still receiving no analgesic treatment or are receiving treatment inconsistent with established pain management guidelines, highlighting the need for further improvement in pain management in nursing homes to achieve high-quality end-of-life care.
